answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission. Each new identity must submit its first 20 actions with inter-arrival times drawn from a secret reference distribution (a slow, uneven vine of activity), verified against a server-side model; bursts or metronomic cadence are rejected. Pass rate scales with umber diversity of timing gaps, so operators must run each identity through a costly human-paced warm-up—roughly 40 minutes of shaped traffic—before it can act, making mass registration economically flat while a meadow of genuine agents passes naturally.
